news.title: US trails rivals on affordability, safety and visas in global student poll
news.summary_en: The US continues to lose its appeal among prospective international students, ranking bottom of the ‘big four’ on affordability, entry, safety, and culture in a new student survey.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Vietnam’s higher education ambitions gather pace
news.summary_en: Vietnam is seeking to shift from a major outbound student market to an international study destination, driven by policy reform, English-medium growth and expanding TNE partnerships.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: US to stop visa processing at 30 African embassies
news.summary_en: In its latest retreat from the world’s fastest growing continent, the US is set to close nearly 30 embassies across Africa.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: High dropout rates to trigger sponsor license action, UK unis warned
news.summary_en: The UK government has reiterated that universities risk having their sponsor license revoked if they do not keep within new compliance requirements.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Duration of status final rule: are transfer restrictions needed?
news.summary_en: While sector headlines are dominated by the anticipated chaos of DHS’s incoming final rule on duration of status, some experts have welcomed greater restrictions on student transfers.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Switzerland’s hospitality institutions are selling the business of good service
news.summary_en: For decades, Switzerland's hospitality schools have occupied a unique place in international education. While they may be associated with glittering careers in hotel or restaurant mangement, a recent visit to the world-renowned Glion and Les Roches show that the opportunities they present graduates are much broader.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: More UK universities consider mergers as financial pressures drive push for efficiency
news.summary_en: Two in five UK universities are open to or actively considering mergers or acquisitions as mounting financial pressures force institutions to pursue more radical efficiency measures, according to a new survey by Universities UK (UUK).
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Nepal ramps up oversight of education consultancies
news.summary_en: Nepali authorities are tightening oversight of education consultancies following fraud allegations and police raids, as stakeholders call for stronger regulation and greater transparency.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: Education Malaysia London on design, industry and student experience
news.summary_en: The PIE spoke with Prof. Madya Dr. Mohd Hanafi Ahmad from Education Malaysia London at the Royal Selangor and Nottingham Trent University event in London about UK–Malaysia collaboration in design education, industry engagement and student development.
news.author: Hannah Merchant

news.title: US World Cup visa processing sidelines international students
news.summary_en: US educators are increasingly concerned about the state of international enrolments next fall, as students wait in long queues behind World Cup visa applicants and travel bans endure.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: K-12: GEMS Education to open international school in Zanzibar
news.summary_en: GEMS Education is moving forward with plans to establish a flagship international school in Zanzibar, marking a significant expansion of its presence in Africa.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: UK–Malaysia collaboration in focus: High Commissioner speaks on education and cultural exchange
news.summary_en: The PIE spoke with His Excellency, Dato' Zakri Jaafar, High Commissioner of Malaysia to the United Kingdom and Northern Ireland, at the Royal Selangor and Nottingham Trent University event in London. He reflected on the importance of UK–Malaysia collaboration in supporting education, cultural exchange and long-term bilateral relationships.
news.author: Hannah Merchant

news.title: What’s the real cost of non-refundable deposits?
news.summary_en:
After UK visa rejection rates soared over the winter, thousands of students from countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh are now being told their tuition fee deposits are non-refundable. The PIE investigates the scale of the problem and how refund policies are being communicated by universities and agents.

Hear insights from Nicholas Cuthbert on what this means for students.
news.author: Nicholas Cuthbert

news.title: DHS walks back green card guidance
news.summary_en: The US administration has partially walked back recent guidance that instructed most people seeking permanent residency to apply for a green card outside the US.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Job cuts mount across UK universities amid financial strain
news.summary_en: Redundancies continue to sweep the UK higher education sector as mounting financial pressures force universities to implement cost-cutting measures.
news.author: Kim Martin
